title: Nanjing's Ming Bricks Are Signed by Their Makers | China Travel Expert
description:
Walk Nanjing's 600-year-old Ming city wall and look closely: the bricks are stamped with their own quality-control records. Each brick carries the place it came from, the official who supervised it, and the name of the maker — so a cracked or weak brick could be traced straight back to one person.

The National Cultural Heritage Administration's UNESCO submission describes this marking system, and heritage guides note it was used to hold makers and supervisors accountable. Built under the founding Ming emperor in the late 1300s, the wall still shows these inscriptions today, and a brick carved with the same characters as the actor Andy Lau's name — a Ming-era brickmaker's — even sits in the Nanjing City Wall Museum.

Expert Tip: at the Nanjing City Wall Museum and along the Zhonghua Gate section, look for the carved characters on the brick faces — that is the 600-year-old 'signature.'
